text:
morgan: heads up, prod alert — decrypt failing for service-account role after yesterday's CMK rotation. getting AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when trying to unwrap envelope keys. :frowning_face:
sam: are these errors coming from assumed-role calls or from the original principal?
morgan: the app assumes role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/data-encryptor via STS. logs show the Decrypt call is made by that role, but KMS returns AccessDenied. CloudTrail entry attached (see timeline).
jamie: can you paste the key policy and the role trust/inline policy? quick check: key policy needs the principal or a blanket AWS account allow for kms:Decrypt. also watch out for session policies that remove kms:Decrypt.
morgan: pasted minimal snippets below — removing sensitive ARNs.
morgan: ```json
{ "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root"},"Action":"kms:*","Resource":"*"},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/rotator"},"Action":["kms:CreateGrant","kms:RetireGrant"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```
morgan: role policy on the assumed role just has kms:Decrypt permission on the key resource.
sam: hmm key policy looks permissive for the account root but not explicitly for the assumed role. If the role is in the same account that root allow should cover it though. Are you seeing a grant token in the decrypt call?
morgan: no grant token shown in app logs. we used a grant during rotation to allow the rotator role to rewrap but that was yesterday morning.
rotator-bot: rotator completed key rotation job at 2025-09-08T03:12:10Z — created new CMK alias alias/enc-prod-2025-09 and created grant G-abc123 for role/rotator with grantToken "gt-xyz". old key scheduled for deletion (kept as replica)
jamie: two common failure modes: 1) the app was issued a ciphertext envelope that references the old CMK id (or encrypt buffer tied to old key) and the decrypt call is hitting the new key (mismatch), or 2) a grant token was used during rotation and not propagated to the calling process — grant tokens are ephemeral and must be passed in the same API call that uses them.
emily: also check session tags/session policy. if the role is assumed with a session policy that strips kms:Decrypt, the allow from IAM won't apply. CloudTrail "AssumeRole" shows sessionPolicy?
morgan: copied CloudTrail lines: Decrypt event = principalArn: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/data-encryptor/ecs-task-123, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer. No sessionPolicy field in assumeRole event.
sam: try a repro from your laptop using aws cli with sts assume-role then aws kms decrypt. show both calls. example: 
sam: ```bash
CREDS=$(aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/data-encryptor --role-session-name test)
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo $CREDS | jq -r .Credentials.AccessKeyId)
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo $CREDS | jq -r .Credentials.SecretAccessKey)
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo $CREDS | jq -r .Credentials.SessionToken)
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --key-id alias/enc-prod-2025-09 --output text
```
morgan: ran that — same AccessDenied. CloudTrail on the decrypt shows errorCode AccessDenied and the keyId points to the new key ARN not the old.
jamie: that suggests ciphertext is already referring to new alias — rewrap step probably issued ciphertext under new CMK for some objects, but the app's role isn't allowed to use the new key. Check that the new key's key policy includes the account/principal. Did the rotator create the new CMK with a restrictive policy?
morgan: rotator created CMK with default autogenerated policy that only allows root and the rotator role to manage, not the app role. I thought we had an account-wide allow in key policies historically.
emily: yep default AWS-created CMK policies can be restrictive. For rotation flow you need to add a statement allowing your consumer principals to use kms:Decrypt for the new key or create grants that persist. Grants created by rotator were targeted at rotator role only.
sam: for immediate fix, either: 1) create a grant on the new key with GranteePrincipal = arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/data-encryptor and Operations ["Decrypt"], or 2) update key policy to include the role (or account) for kms:Decrypt. Grant is the least intrusive short-term.
morgan: tried creating grant: `aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/enc-prod-2025-09 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/data-encryptor --operations Decrypt` returned GrantId and now decrypt from cli works. app still fails though.
sam: app may be running with cached credentials or using a library that pins key id. Check env and restart tasks. Also verify the app isn't using old grant token flow — it must either use the grant id locally, or just rely on IAM/key policy allow.
morgan: restarted tasks, now decrypts succeed. :grin:
jamie: good. follow-up: update key policy creator flow to include app roles during automated CMK creation, or modify rotator to add cross-reference statements post-creation. Also audit all other services for similar failures.
emily: add a test in rotator CI: after creating CMK, call `aws kms test-iam-permissions --key-id <new> --permissions kms:Decrypt` with creds of a sample consumer role. That will catch missing allows.
ops-bot: ticket #INF-4123 created: "Ensure CMK creation includes consumer principals or grants" assigned to eng-security, priority P2.
morgan: quick note for posterity: grant tokens are easy to mis-use — they only matter during the API call that creates the grant or immediately after. For cross-process handoff prefer either persistent grant or key-policy allow.
sam: also re-encrypt path: for files encrypted under old key, we rewrapped to new key in rotation job. If we didn't rewrap some objects then consumers might still try to decrypt with the new key and fail if they lack access to the old key. double-check for mixed-key ciphertexts.
morgan: will run inventory to find ciphertexts referencing old-key-id and rewrap if needed. closing once inventory + policy change done. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
emily: ping me if you want me to own the policy change PR.
morgan: assigned to emily, will keep this thread updated.
